steps.name: QC and count matrix preparation
caveats: RSEM expected counts are non-integer; round before feeding into count-based DE tools rather than truncating, to avoid systematic downward bias
The genes.results files with effective gene lengths are not available, so no length-offset correction is possible here — note this explicitly as a limitation, do not attempt to approximate it
steps.question: What are the library size distributions across the 12 colon samples (6 treated, 6 control), and how severe is the sample_01 shallow-library issue relative to the rest of the cohort?
acceptance_criteria: Reports total library size (column sums) per sample from counts.csv, ranked, with sample_01's rank and fold-deviation from median made explicit
Rounds RSEM expected counts to nearest integer and confirms all values are non-negative integers post-rounding
Flags any other samples with library size outliers using a simple threshold (e.g., >2x median absolute deviation) besides sample_01
Produces a merged, sample-annotated count matrix (genes x 12 samples) with condition labels from metadata.csv, saved for downstream steps

steps.name: Primary DE: treated vs control, all 12 samples
caveats: Unpaired single-batch design means no batch covariate is needed, but do not add one that doesn't exist in metadata
n=6 per group is modest power; do not overstate significance of borderline hits

sample_01's low library size can inflate its dispersion contribution; DESeq2's default size-factor normalization should partially compensate but does not fully correct the effect of a 4x-fold difference
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated (n=6) and control (n=6) colon samples using the full 12-sample cohort?
acceptance_criteria: Runs pydeseq2 with condition (treated vs control) as the sole factor on the rounded integer count matrix from T1S1
Reports full DE results table (log2FC, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value/padj) for all ~12000 genes
Applies standard significance thresholds (padj < 0.05, |log2FC| > 1) and reports counts of up/down genes at that threshold
Includes size-factor / normalization diagnostics per sample so sample_01's estimated size factor can be inspected against its raw library size

steps.name: Sensitivity DE: treated vs control excluding sample_01
caveats: Removing sample_01 drops the design to an unbalanced 5v6 or exactly 5v5 depending which arm it belongs to — report which, since it affects power symmetry
This is a sensitivity check, not a replacement primary analysis — report both results, do not silently prefer one
steps.question: Do the treated-vs-control DE results change materially when the shallow-library sample_01 is excluded (5 vs 6 or 5 vs 5 depending on sample_01's condition)?
acceptance_criteria: Identifies sample_01's condition label (treated or control) from metadata.csv before exclusion
Re-runs pydeseq2 on the remaining 11 samples with the same model as T1S2
Reports the same padj<0.05, |log2FC|>1 gene set and up/down counts for the reduced cohort

Directly compares the T1S2 (all 12) and T1S3 (11, sample_01 excluded) significant gene lists: overlap count, genes lost, genes gained, and Spearman/Pearson correlation of log2FC across all genes tested in both

steps.name: Pathway enrichment on robust DE gene set
caveats: Only WikiPathways human is confirmed present as an organism-matched pathway reference in this environment; no MSigDB Hallmark/KEGG/Reactome collection was found — report enrichment findings as WikiPathways-only coverage, not a comprehensive pathway scan
Gene symbol matching between the RSEM count matrix's gene identifiers and the GMT's HGNC symbols should be checked for overlap rate before interpreting a null enrichment result as biological absence
steps.question: Which biological pathways are enriched among the genes robustly differentially expressed between treated and control colon samples (significant in both the full-cohort and sample_01-excluded analyses)?
acceptance_criteria: Defines the 'robust' DE gene set as the intersection of T1S2 and T1S3 significant genes (padj<0.05, |log2FC|>1); reports its size explicitly
Runs over-representation or GSEA-style enrichment against the WikiPathways human gene sets (organism-matched, HGNC symbols) confirmed present in the environment
Reports enriched pathways with adjusted p-values (BH), ranked, for both up- and down-regulated robust gene subsets separately
If the robust gene set is empty or too small (<5 genes) for meaningful enrichment, reports this explicitly rather than forcing an enrichment run on the full unfiltered DE list

plan.title: Colon RNA-seq treated vs control DE with QC gating
plan.analytical_narrative: The input is a bulk RNA-seq (RSEM gene-level expected counts) matrix from human colon tissue, 12000 genes x 12 samples, 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. The counts are non-integer RSEM expected counts (a known DESeq2-compatible input via round()), and the per-sample genes.results files with effective gene lengths were not delivered, so no length-based renormalization (e.g. tximport-style offset) is possible — length bias from RSEM must be accepted as a limitation rather than corrected. Sample sample_01 has a library size ~4x below the median, which is a QC flag for exclusion or careful handling rather than something to normalize away silently. The plan therefore: (1) profiles library sizes and rounds/prepares the count matrix, flagging sample_01 explicitly and testing DE both with and without it to assess sensitivity; (2) runs DESeq2 (via pydeseq2, since it's the confirmed-present Python engine) for the primary treated-vs-control contrast on the full 12-sample set with library size as a covariate consideration, plus a sensitivity re-run excluding sample_01; (3) compares the two DE gene lists to report which findings are robust to the outlier sample; (4) runs pathway enrichment on the robust DE gene set using WikiPathways human gene sets, the only pathway reference confirmed present and organism-matched. No translational/clinical/PK steps are added since the research question is a plain DE contrast with no drug, biomarker, or outcome data in scope.
